title: This is my very first game. Just making it to the Steam Wishlist stage is my biggest pride so far! 📼
author: GoatNo466
selftext:
I’m a solo dev from LATAM, and I've been pouring my heart into VHS Store Tycoon.

I know the harsh reality of indie dev: most first-time projects never even make it to having a Steam page. So, finally getting to this stage after facing so many technical challenges as a beginner is a huge personal milestone and something I am incredibly proud of.

It’s a 90s retro management game made in Godot 4. If you like nostalgia and Tycoon games, checking it out and adding it to your wishlist would mean the absolute world to me. Every single wishlist helps this solo dream survive the Steam algorithm!

[VHS STORE TYCOON ON STEAM](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4880040/)

Thank you for reading 👾📼

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
I don't know why people are obsessed with sticking their first half finished vibe coded game on Steam.

All your images in the game look like obvious AI generated art, the UI looks very unpolished and you don't seem to have even basic pixel art game dev knowledge as your character sprites look blurred. 

If you want to make something good spend another 6 months on it.

Also this game already exists as a 3D version and is far better. Why would someone want to play a worse pixel version?

replies.author: GoatNo466
replies.body:
I understand your point, and I want to thank you for taking the time to comment.



I know it has AI, and I know there are a few tweaks needed, but they’re minor—I still have a few days left, and I’ll fix them. Keep in mind that this is my first video game; even though I’m trying to make it as good as possible, I’m going to make mistakes, so that’s what I’m working on—improving every day... You’re probably right about the 3D game you mentioned, but keep in mind that not everyone can play it— not everyone has a PC that can run it. A 2D pixel art version isn’t bad. I’ll have a demo soon, and I’d like to invite you to play it and draw your own conclusions. And although your comment feels like constructive criticism, it also comes across as a bit condescending. In that case, I suppose you must at least have a finished product on Steam—I’d like to check it out and learn more that way. Thanks.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
Slapping something on Steam is not an indication of a good game. Anyone can put something on Steam if they are willing to pay the fee. That's why I think it's weird people are obsessed with doing it. I could literally spend the afternoon slapping together an asset flip and add it to Steam. It's not any kind of achievement.

My criticism might seem harsh but if you're not going to even learn the basics of using pixel art in games why do you expect people to play it or pay for it. Even if you hadn't used any AI this would still be a low effort game. It's the kind of game people would usually make as a learning experience not something they would put on Steam. 

If you want to make something good and not something that's going to instantly fall into the AI slop category with the thousands of other AI slop games people are currently uploading everywhere then you need to spend time and also learn some of the basics. Building a game like this that is going to look polished and appealing would normally take a competent game dev several months or even years depending on how much of the work they outsourced. AI isn't a skip button to success.

Anyway good luck with it.
